name: Two.js
role: Scene graph for flat 2D drawing with one API across SVG, Canvas and WebGL renderers
summary: Dependency-free 2D drawing API with a scene graph, built-in animation loop and three interchangeable renderers (SVG, Canvas, WebGL). Includes an SVG interpreter for importing artwork from tools like Illustrator. Output is SVG DOM, Canvas or WebGL pixels. Its strength is writing a scene once and choosing the renderer, SVG included.
use_when: Flat geometry that must be output as SVG or Canvas from the same code
Over Paper.js when you want a simple scene graph and renderer choice, not path booleans
Importing Illustrator SVG into a scripted, animated scene
Over PixiJS when the scene is small and vector-first
avoid_when: Many sprites or GPU filters: PixiJS
Seekable timelines on DOM or SVG: GSAP
Interactive object editing: Konva or Fabric.js
notes: 2026-10-26: two.js.org did not describe SVG export; only SVG import was confirmed.

assessment.rationale: GitHub release v0.8.24 on 2026-08-29; MIT, copyright 2012-2026. Renderer-agnostic scene graph is its distinct angle versus Paper.js and PixiJS.
